This petition coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER 1.

This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed seeking the following reliefs :-

(i) That, it is therefore, prayed before this Hon'ble Court may kindly issue appropriate Writ and set aside impugned order dated 29/11/2011 (Annexure-P/7) in the interest of justice.

(ii) That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to direct to the respondent no. 2 &
3 to determine Compensation to the petitioner by assuming land of the petitioner irrigated land and also include the land Khasra no. 487 Bashar no. 208 for determination of compensation in the interest of justice.
(iii) That, this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to call entire records.
(iv) That, any other relief which this Hon'ble Court may deemed fit and proper on the basis of above mentioned facts and grounds.

2. It is submitted by counsel for the petitioner that certain lands of the petitioner were acquired but the petitioner was not satisfied with the compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer,
therefore, he filed an application before the Collector, Rewa for enhancement of compensation.
In the said application, it was also prayed that Khasra no. 487 has not been acquired.

3. Since that application was pending and was not decided, the petitioner filed a W.P.No.16376/2011 which was disposed of by order dated 1.10.2011 with liberty to the petitioner to file a fresh application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of the said order and it was directed that the Collector, Rewa shall decide the application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in accordance with law.
4. It is submitted that now, the Collector, Rewa by the impugned order dated 29.11.2011 passed in case no. 2/A/82/2011-12 has rejected the application on the ground of limitation.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
6.

Although the petitioner has not filed a copy of the application which was filed in compliance of the order dated 1.10.2011 passed in W.P.No. 16376/2011 but the same was provided by the petitioner for perusal of this Court.
7. Counsel for the petitioner has also admitted that the petitioner has not disclosed the date of knowledge of the award in the said application.
It is also conceded by counsel for the petitioner that the question of non- acquisition of Khasra no. 487 has also not been raised in the said application.

8. Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, reads as under :-
"18.
Reference to Court.

- (1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the Ramsiya Tiwari (Dead) Through Lrs ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38410085/
2 measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the person to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested.

sentences.text:
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
Provided that every such application shall be made- (a) if the person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collector's award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 12, sub-section (2), or within six months from the date of the Collector's award, whichever period shall first expire."
9. From plain reading of the aforesaid section, it is clear that application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has to be filed within a period of 6 months from the date of knowledge of award.
The petitioner had not disclosed the date of knowledge of award in his application.
10. Under these circumstances, the Collector, Rewa did not commit any mistake by rejecting the application as barred by time.

In absence of any provision for condonation of delay, the Collector,
Rewa was also unable to condone the delay.

As no illegality was committed by the Collector,
therefore, order dated 29.11.2011 passed in case no. 2/A/82/2011-12 is hereby affirmed.
11. The petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
